page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.10xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 40 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 20 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 35 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.4 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

In synthetic benchmarks, the ecs.hfc6.10xlarge demonstrates solid compute capabilities, achieving a Passmark CPU score of 34,144.54 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 11,735.0. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only cached small-block bandwidth of 2,132.58 GB/sec and an uncached large-block write speed of 36.66 GB/sec. The processor's instruction set efficiency is reflected in a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 161.64 GB/sec and a static web serving throughput of 23.2 GB/sec. For database workloads, the instance processes 34.66 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 13,891.08 on Passmark database operations.

Given its high-frequency dedicated Intel Xeon processor and compute-heavy resource ratio, the ecs.hfc6.10xlarge is designed for workloads requiring sustained CPU performance without massive memory footprints. It is highly suitable for web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a cost-efficient choice for pure compute tasks, such as batch processing and lightweight LLM inference, where the 7B model achieves 12.33 tokens per second for text generation.
